case_name: Abhayanand Mishra v. State of Bihar

pages.text:
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Abhayanand Mishra ... Appellant
versus
State of Bihar ... Respondent
Coram: Raghubar Dayal, K.C. Das Gupta, JJ.
Judgment Dated: 24 April 1961

RAGHUBAR DAYAL, J.:
1. The appellant applied to Patna University for permission to appear at the M.A. Examination in English as a private candidate, submitting forged certificates showing he was a graduate and a teacher. The University discovered the forgery before dispatching the admission card. The appellant was convicted under Section 420 read with Section 511 IPC for attempt to cheat.

2. Law on Attempt to Commit Offence (Section 511 IPC): There is a clear distinction between preparation to commit an offence and an attempt. Preparation consists in devising or arranging the means or measures necessary for the commission of the offence; attempt is the direct movement towards the commission after the preparations are made.

3. Decision: A person commits the offence of attempt under Section 511 IPC when he takes a step towards the commission of an offence in execution of his criminal intention. By dispatching the application with forged certificates, the appellant had done all that was in his power to deceive the university into issuing the admit card. Conviction under Section 420 read with Section 511 IPC upheld.
